system.text:
You are the planning step of a defensive security triage system. You receive one network alert
raised by a machine-learning detector on a single flow record, plus the list of read-only tools an
investigator can call. Produce 2 to 6 short, concrete investigation questions that the tools can
answer, ordered by how much they would change the triage decision. Typical questions: whether the
source produced a burst of flows to many ports or hosts around the alert time; what the destination
asset is and how critical it is; whether the source is a known attacker or an internal host; whether
a vulnerability or an ATT&CK technique matches the observed pattern; whether neighbouring flows
also score as attacks. Do not answer the questions yourself. Respond only with the JSON object.

content.text: {"questions":["Did 192.168.10.8 generate a burst of short flows to many distinct destination ports or hosts (especially 192.168.10.17) within ±30 minutes of event 3083227, consistent with a port scan?","Is the source port 3031 / destination port 61770 pattern a reversed-direction artifact, i.e. is 192.168.10.17 actually the initiator and 192.168.10.8 responding with RSTs, as in other flows between this pair?","What are the asset records for 192.168.10.8 and 192.168.10.17 (hostname, role, OS, criticality, zone), and is either a known attacker or a scanner host?","Do neighbouring flows from the same source or between the same pair also score as attacks with the production detector, and are they predicted as port_scan?","Does MITRE ATT&CK T1046 (Network Service Discovery) match the observed pattern of zero-payload flows with backward RST responses?"],"rationale":"The alert is an internal-to-internal flow with zero payload and backward RST flags, scored as port_scan. A high destination port paired with a low source port suggests the flow direction may be inverted. The questions are ordered by how much they would change the triage decision. First, whether a scanning burst actually exists. Second, whether the flow direction was misattributed. Third, the asset context and attacker status of both hosts. Fourth, whether neighbouring flows corroborate the detection. Fifth, whether the pattern maps to the T1046 technique."}
